question: A 2-year-old child is a household contact of a smear-positive pulmonary TB patient. Mantoux test shows 4 mm induration. Chest X-ray is normal. There are no symptoms. What is the most appropriate next step under NTEP guidelines?

answers.text: Initiate full anti-TB treatment (2HRZE + 4HRE) as household contact of smear-positive case

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Full ATT is indicated only if the child has active TB disease. This child has no symptoms, normal CXR, and negative TST — criteria for IPT, not full treatment.

answers.text: Reassure the family, observe for 3 months, and repeat Mantoux

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. In a child under 5 years who is a household contact of a smear-positive case, waiting and watching without chemoprophylaxis is not appropriate even if the Mantoux is negative.

answers.text: Initiate Isoniazid Preventive Therapy (IPT) with 6 months of isoniazid

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Under NTEP, all children under 5 years who are household contacts of smear-positive TB patients should receive IPT (isoniazid chemoprophylaxis for 6 months), regardless of Mantoux result, provided active TB has been excluded. The Mantoux threshold for IPT eligibility is ≥5 mm in immunocompromised children; however, under-5 contacts get IPT irrespective of TST.
Incorrect. BCG is given at birth for primary prevention. It is not used as post-exposure prophylaxis after TB contact. IPT with isoniazid is the correct chemoprophylaxis for under-5 contacts.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the IPT section. Key rule: ALL children under 5 years who are household contacts of smear-positive TB patients → exclude active TB → start IPT (6 months isoniazid), regardless of Mantoux result.
Correct. Under NTEP, children under 5 years who are household contacts of smear-positive TB receive IPT (6 months isoniazid) once active TB is excluded, regardless of Mantoux result.
